idiom_name: row class with insert/load/update methods over SOCI or the SQLite C API
implementation_notes: The row class and its persistence methods are hand-written; what a library contributes is value mapping, not the pattern. SOCI's object-relational support binds columns directly into members (into(p)) and parameters out of them (use(x)) inside an ordinary C++ class, and the SQLite C API gives the same with prepare/bind/step. What replaces the framework-provided CRUD of scripting ORMs is a small wrapper layer - one method per operation, primary-key-driven - and the classic form is justified while the schema is small and stable; with several tables or representations, a mapper or a query builder (sqlite_orm, ODB, SOCI row types) pays off sooner because C++ has no decorators or reflection to derive the mapping from.
pitfalls: SQL string literals inside the class tie it to one dialect and schema; without a migration-checked mapping they drift silently from the database.
Row objects returned by value slice away derived behaviour if the hierarchy is polymorphic; store the record type by value and keep polymorphism elsewhere.
Per-object round trips (load one row, save one row, then follow the association) produce N+1 traffic; batch explicitly when the graph is loaded in bulk.
